question: A flower bouquet contains pink roses, red roses, pink carnations, and red carnations. One third of the pink flowers are roses, three fourths of the red flowers are carnations, and six tenths of the flowers are pink. What percent of the flowers are carnations?
solution:
Find the fraction of all flowers that are carnations in each color group. Since \(\frac13\) of the pink flowers are roses, the remaining \(\frac23\) are carnations. Pink flowers make up \(\frac6{10}=\frac35\) of the bouquet, so pink carnations make up
\[
\frac35\cdot\frac23=\frac25
\]
of all flowers.

The remaining \(\frac25\) of the flowers are red. Since \(\frac34\) of those are carnations, red carnations make up
\[
\frac25\cdot\frac34=\frac3{10}
\]
of all flowers. Every carnation is either pink or red, and these groups do not overlap. Therefore the fraction of carnations is
\[
\frac25+\frac3{10}
=\frac4{10}+\frac3{10}
=\frac7{10}=70\%.
\]
The answer is \(70\%\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).

edges.reason: Once denominators agree, the target adds or subtracts numerators in equal fractional units, directly using same-denominator arithmetic.
The target explicitly first rewrites unlike denominators to a common denominator. That renaming step is a required procedure here, regardless of other possible fraction-addition representations.

The integer-multiplier case supplies a useful stepping stone and repeated-addition interpretation. The product-of-numerators/product-of-denominators rule follows directly from a part-of-a-part area model without executing the earlier decimal-free integer-multiplier procedure; Gemini confuses this customary progression with necessity.

The endpoint provides explicit quantity-modeling experience that can help translate a fraction-of-a-whole story into an expression. Price and speed formulas do not define a fractional part, so the benefit is preparation only. This final scoped judgment does not treat a prior native acceptance of Claude's rejection as an accepted dependency.
edges.scope: Prior experience representing total, part and multiplicative relationships in application problems

edges.reason: Taking a fraction of a fractional quantity contains a fraction-by-fraction product in the full application repertoire.

The percent criterion explicitly represents the multiplicative relation between two numbers. A hundredths fraction represents that same quotient comparison; avoiding formal ratio terminology does not remove the relation itself. Require only this shared meaning, not prior completion of ratio exercises or notation.
edges.scope: The quotient meaning of the multiplicative comparison between two quantities

edges.reason: The hundredths-to-decimal correspondence is directly used in percent/decimal conversion. Only that conversion component is required, not every fraction/decimal conversion exercise.
edges.scope: percent to decimal and back via hundredths

edges.reason: Writing a percent as hundredths uses what the percent sign means as a relative quantity per hundred.
edges.scope: converting between percents, fractions and decimals
